# Joint family and its businesses — the Randhawa family (seven books) — technical companion (FY 2025-26)

**Status: ⚠️ PROVISIONAL — pending bookkeeper sign-off.** Generated by `build.py` beside the printed report `joint-family-randhawa.md` (`.html`, `.pdf`); never edited by hand. The printed report carries the user's plain words with the true side in brackets (ADR 2026-10-12 §2, ADR 2026-10-10b §4); this file carries the engine view of the **same entries and the same figures**: classes, kinds, refs, review and advance states, the rules the scenario exercises, the ⚠️ SPEC readings that apply, and the checks. `fixtures.json` is the machine copy; `README.md` is the reading guide.

Entity: Joint family: one joint fund, three sub-family books, three family businesses. Books: `RF` Randhawa Family Fund — Joint Fund Book (97 vouchers, TB ₹14,19,387.10); `AF` Amarjeet's Family — Sub-family Book (68 vouchers, TB ₹2,53,900); `LF` Lakhbeer's Family — Sub-family Book (66 vouchers, TB ₹2,71,800); `LW` Lakhwinder's Family — Sub-family Book (79 vouchers, TB ₹3,40,600); `RA` Randhawa Agriculture — Family Business Book (138 vouchers, TB ₹22,16,600.34); `RR` Randhawa Real Estate — Family Business Book (111 vouchers, TB ₹5,55,000); `RB` Randhawa Brick Field — Shared Business Book (155 vouchers, TB ₹29,17,000).

## 3. Vouchers — `kind`, lines, refs and states (02 §1.3, §1.4 rule 7)

Lines are signed paise, + = Dr, − = Cr, on the account id of §2; a tag in brackets is the appropriation line tag (`interest` / `share`). *Authored* is shown only when it differs from the accounting date. The printed day book shows the same entries as *Money in / Money out / Gave on credit / Took on credit / Transfer / Correction / adjustment* and prints the narration without its rule citation.

## 5. ⚠️ SPEC readings that apply here (README §5 has all twelve)

- **S1 · kind of the advance postings.** 02 §7 prescribes the postings (`Dr Advance · Cr money`; `Dr expense · Cr Advance`; `Dr money · Cr Advance`; write-off `Dr Adjustments · Cr Advance`) and ADR 2026-09-05e §6 calls the advance shape already reader-checked, but neither names the `kind` (02 §1.3 lists six). This set labels by nearest shape — request and spend `money_out`, return `money_in`, write-off `adjustment` — which is also how the engine's `checkShape` admits them.
- **S2 · kind of the partner postings.** 02 §7.1's three events name postings, not kinds: own-pocket `Dr Expense · Cr Partner Current` is `took_credit`, takeout `Dr Partner Current · Cr money` is `money_out` (the engine treats `partner` as party-like), and the appropriation `Dr Profit Distributed · Cr each Partner Current` is one `adjustment` (exactly one `equity_system` counter-account, rule 7).
- **S3 · kinds of the one-sided inter-book case.** 02 §6 calls *a member pays a family expense from his own pocket* the same mechanism as a transfer and ADR 2026-09-05e §6 admits *the §6 pair shapes*. The payer half `Dr link · Cr Cash` is a `transfer`; the payee half `Dr Expense · Cr link` is read as a **`money_out`** whose credit is the link — the engine's `money_out` arm admits a Due credit and its `transfer` arm admits only money and Due. Both halves share one `transfer_group`.
- **S5 · accounting date of an approved advance request.** 02 §7 posts the request *on approval* and 02 §1.4 rule 4 makes entries immutable; this set keeps the request date as the accounting date (RA June: requested 10 Jun, approved 12 Jun, excluded from every balance in between, counted from 10 Jun once approved). If the owner prefers the approval date, only the ledger row's date moves.
- **S6 · ageing method.** 02 §7 defines advance ageing as *days since the oldest unsettled debit*; 07 §7 gives party chips (> 30 amber, > 90 red) without a matching rule. This set reads both as **FIFO**: credits settle the oldest open debits first and an unapplied credit (deposit, prepayment) offsets the next debit. Consequence shown in Real Estate: a tenant's arrears only *show* as Dr once they exceed the deposit held.
- **S8 · an owner who is not on the app.** The Brick Field's `structural_quorum` is `all_owners` (chosen at creation, 02 §7.2.1); Nirmaljeet Gill holds no device, so no signed approval can exist for him and no structural action — profit distribution, interest, ratio change — can complete in-app. This set leaves the surplus undistributed and carried; the owner must rule how an off-app owner approves (a paper mandate recorded by an admin? a required invite?).
- **S11 · count timing.** Cash is counted at close of business on the month's last day, any difference is dated that day, and the lock follows a few days later — so the certified month ends on counted cash (02 §8 step 1). A count performed on the lock day itself would date the adjustment in the next month; both are consistent with 02 §8.
- **S12 · link account naming.** 02 §6 names the engine's accounts *Due to/from {Book}*; the owner ruled plain labels for this set. The class is unchanged (`equity_system`, role link) and the name carries the other book and its type, e.g. *Randhawa Family Fund (joint family book)*.

Readings this scenario was built to exercise: accounting date of an approved advance request = the request date; Brick Field quorum unreachable in-app.

## 6. Developer notes kept off the printed report

- **Conventions.** Amounts in ₹ with paise shown only when non-zero; the engine holds integer paise. Ledgers follow the standards §2 layout — Date · Particulars (To … on the debit side, By … on the credit side) · contextual Dr · contextual Cr · Balance · Side on every row — and, being printed ledgers, end *Closing balance c/d · Total · Opening balance b/d* with no separate c/f row (ADR 2026-09-24b §9). Income and expense ledgers carry no b/f row and are not carried forward (ADR 2026-09-05e §2). The printed column headers are the plain words with the true side in brackets (ADR 2026-10-10b §4); the engine's posting logic never bends to the display language (02 §10).
- **Openings.** One adjustment per account against Opening Balance / Capital (02 §4; the engine's `Verbs.openingBalance`), dated at the book start (ADR 2026-09-09d §4); the narration's citation *(02 §4; counterpart …)* prints as *(set against …)*.
- **Year close** (02 §8.1, ADR 2026-09-05e §2): the certified closing vector carries money, party, advance, partner and equity_system accounts as on 31 Mar 2026; category accounts are not carried; the net result is one line; *Accumulated surplus* is a computed line (02 §1.2), printed as *Family's own funds (accumulated surplus) / Owner's funds in the business (accumulated surplus) / Partners' funds in the business (accumulated surplus)*; there is no closing journal entry; every member's device recomputes the same vector (02 §8 step 4). Preconditions asserted: all 12 months locked · Suspense 0 · no open review flag · no pending advance request (the sync-layer checks of ADR 2026-09-05e §4 are outside this reference's scope).
- **Position** = 07 §14 *Full Position*, by sign (02 §1.2): every carried account on the side its balance says; the printed heading is *What I/we have and what I/we owe (position)*.
- **Periods** (02 §8): step 1 cash counts at close of business on the month's last day, differences `Dr/Cr Cash · Cr/Dr Adjustments` (kind `adjustment`, tag `count_diff`); step 3 tray at the lock — Suspense, open flags, pending advances; aged advances warn only (reminder default 15 days).

### Tenants — RR, ageing reading (⚠️ SPEC S6)

Each tenant is one party account (02 §1.2: one party, one account). A security deposit is a credit; monthly rent is a debit on the 1st; a receipt credits it. Ageing reading (⚠️ SPEC S6): receipts settle the oldest open debits first (FIFO); an unapplied credit — a deposit — offsets the next debit, so a tenant's arrears only *show* as a Dr once they exceed the deposit held. This is a modelling consequence of one-party-one-account that the owner should see: Dr Kaur's Clinic could be three months behind and still read Cr. Sharma Family hold no deposit, so their arrears are visible and age plainly. The 07 §7 chip turns amber after 30 days and red after 90.

### Brick Field — RB, off-app owner (⚠️ SPEC S8)

No profit distribution and no interest on capital this year: both are structural actions (02 §7.2.1) needing a quorum of owners' signed approvals, and Nirmaljeet Gill is not on the app, so no approval envelope can exist for him. The year's surplus is carried undistributed in the computed *Accumulated surplus* line; the owner should rule how an off-app owner approves (README ⚠️ SPEC S8). The Randhawa family took nothing out this year (the receiving-book side of a partner takeout is unruled — README §6); Gill's takeouts are ordinary partner postings (`Dr Partner Current · Cr money`, kind `money_out`, S2).

### Family Reconciliation — 02 §6

For every pair, balance(A→B) + balance(B→A) = 0 — the only cross-book integrity check that exists or is needed (standards §5.4). The link accounts are `equity_system · link` (S12: named in plain words). 02 §6/§7.1 route business surplus through these pairs rather than through an income account, so the fund's own P&L shows only its common spending. The one-sided own-pocket case (RF-037 ↔ AF-028) is S3.

### Partner settlement routes — RB

Route 1 — business pays out a partner's balance (`Dr Partner Current · Cr bank`): offered; needs cash. Route 2 — partner-to-partner settlement outside the business (`Dr over-funded partner · Cr under-funded partner`): offered; not taken. Route 3 — carry forward (preselected, taken): every partner balance closes and re-opens under the year-close ceremony as a certified, dated opening balance (02 §7.1, 02 §8.1). Drift card margin ₹1,00,000 (07 §7 partner card, informational).

## 7. Checks

- **What `build.py` asserts on every run, and refuses to write otherwise:** every voucher sums to zero with ≥ 2 non-zero lines; every account belongs to its book; the class-shape of every `kind` (02 §1.4 rule 7 as the engine's `checkShape` reads it, incl. the advance, partner and §6 shapes); every trial balance balances; every inter-book pair has two halves of the same date and amount whose link lines mirror, and every pair nets to 0; Opening Balance / Capital exactly once per book; Drawings only in a one-owner business book and partner accounts only in a shared one; capital introduced is `Dr money · Cr Opening Balance / Capital` and never income (ADR 2026-09-13 §4); an owner takeout is `Dr Drawings · Cr money` and never an expense (ADR 2026-09-09b §3); nothing leaves a collection box except a Transfer to cash or bank and nothing enters it except a count, whose *counted by* and *witness* are two different people (02 §8.2); nothing is dated before the start and nothing is authored into a locked month or before its own accounting date; an entry over its author's limit carries a review flag decided by a different admin/head before the lock, a rejected one has its mirror reversal, and only an admin or head amends or reverses (06 §1.0); an advance request is approved by a different admin/head before the lock and no advance account goes negative; Suspense is 0, no flag is open and no advance is pending as of every lock date; every cash account is counted in every month before its lock (trust: with a denomination sheet that sums to the count); the appropriation is one entry whose `interest` lines equal an independent recomputation (half-up to the paisa, credit days only, Actual/365) and whose `share` lines equal the floor-by-weight split with the remainder on the largest weight (ties to the earliest-created account); the closing vector carries only balance-sheet classes and sums to zero with the net line; no cash, collection, savings or current account is negative after any posting; and the printed report carries no engine class, verb id, rule or ADR reference, ⚠️ note, backtick or generator check (`plain_lint`, ADR 2026-10-12 §2).
- **Mutation check** — `python3 build.py --self-test` rebuilds the set in memory, changes one guarded posting at a time (the remainder moved to the wrong partner; an interest line a paisa short; an interest figure not from credit-day balances; capital introduced credited to income; an owner takeout debited to an expense; a gollak count whose witness is the counter; a Transfer into the gollak; an operator amending; an entry authored before its date; the pocket-expense half labelled `transfer`; a Suspense line left uncleared; cash driven negative) and reports whether the validator refused each one. All refusals are expected; a *not refused* line is a defect in the generator.
- **Independent re-derivation** — `check_md.py` parses the printed markdown as a reader would (daybook → ledgers → trial balance → income and expense statement → position → year-close vector, plus the section order and the plain-language lint); this build passed **6794 checks with 0 differences** across the seven printed reports.
